description:
We’re a team of curious people participating in Nasa Space Apps Challenge 2026 :) We’re interested in space exploration, science, technology, and using funny creative ideas to solve real-world problems.

Our project is Lunar Landing Site Navigator, focused on helping identify and explore potential landing sites on the Moon. We want to turn complex lunar data into something useful, accessible, and fun to use.
summary:
LUNA — Lunar Landing Site Navigator

LUNA (Lunar Landing Site Navigator) is a web-based lunar mission planning and visual platform designed to help researchers, scientists, and space mission planners explore potential Moon landing sites using NASA terrain data and orbital calculations.

The project combines NASA Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) elevation data with NASA/JPL NAIF SPICE to analyze lunar terrain, solar illumination, Earth visibility, and environmental conditions that influence landing-site suitability.

Selecting a suitable lunar landing site requires understanding multiple factors, including surface slope, elevation, sunlight availability, Earth communication visibility, and mission timing. Analyzing these factors often requires specialized datasets and scientific tools.
Our solution

LUNA brings these capabilities together into an interactive website where users can explore lunar locations, visualize terrain in 3D, configure mission dates, and compare potential landing scenarios.
Key features
- Interactive mission planner
- 3D lunar terrain: Visualize terrain using NASA LOLA elevation datasets.
- Sun and Earth visibility: Calculate visibility conditions using SPICE orbital geometry and terrain horizons.
- Landing-site assessment: Evaluate terrain slope, sunlight exposure, Earth line of sight, and screening criteria.
- Scenario comparison
- Scientific data integration
details:
LUNA integrates NASA's Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) datasets with NASA/JPL NAIF SPICE orbital geometry calculations to help users evaluate potential lunar landing locations.

The platform allows users to explore lunar terrain in 3D, select landing coordinates, configure mission dates, analyze solar illumination and Earth visibility, and compare potential landing scenarios.

Our objective is to transform complex lunar science datasets into an accessible decision-support tool for researchers, students, engineers, and future space explorers.

Key Capabilities

  • 3D Lunar Terrain Visualization: Interactive exploration using NASA LOLA elevation data.
  • Solar Illumination Analysis: Calculation of Sun position, visibility, and estimated sunlight availability.
  • Earth Communication Visibility: Geometric analysis of Earth line-of-sight conditions.
  • Landing Suitability Screening: Evaluation of terrain elevation, slope, illumination, and communication visibility.
  • Mission Scenario Comparison: Comparison of different landing coordinates, mission dates, and environmental conditions.
  • Scientific Data Integration: Incorporation of NASA terrain datasets, uncertainty information, and orbital calculations.
